correctness.rationale: For each integer \(m\ge2\), the vertex description from the defining inequalities gives exactly the origin, \(m\) vertices \(2e_i\), and \(m(m-1)\) vertices \(2e_i+e_j\). The candidate ellipsoid has two explicitly positive shape eigenvalues. Projection onto the all-ones line gives exact gauges \(q_O=q_B=1\) and \(q_A=1\) for \(m\le5\); for \(m\ge6\), \(1-q_A=4(m-5)(m+1)/(9m(5m-9))>0\). The listed nonnegative probabilities sum to one, have mean \(t\mathbf1\), and covariance \(Q/m\); this is reconstructed algebraically from each orbit's sums and squared norms. For any competing enclosing ellipsoid with center \(b\) and shape \(R\), averaging its containment inequalities yields \(\operatorname{tr}(R^{-1}Q)/m+(t\mathbf1-b)^{\mathsf T}R^{-1}(t\mathbf1-b)\le1\). Eigenvalue AM–GM gives \(\det R\ge\det Q\), and equality forces identical center and shape. Finite exact rational checks for \(2\le m\le100\) and independent complete moment/vertex checks for \(2\le m\le15\) corroborate the all-dimensional proof; they are not infinite proofs. No unproved nonstandard lemma or unstated optimization assumption remains.

value.rationale: The minimum-volume enclosing ellipsoid and exact contact set are natural metric-affine invariants of a named lattice-polytope family. The all-dimensional rational solution exposes a genuine sharp loss of \(m\) support contacts between dimension five and dimension six while the body remains full-dimensional; it is not a renamed known radius or finite table. The orbit probability weights provide explicit determinant optimality certificates that can be reused to benchmark ellipsoidal approximation procedures. Only the second partial permutohedron is treated, an intrinsically motivated canonical fixed-parameter subfamily.
